cards.text: This is a psalm of Asaph, chief of the worship leaders King David appointed (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). It opens with God presiding in the divine assembly. Friend, I thought the Millers' kitchen got serious when somebody touched the last cookie, but THIS is a meeting.

cards.question: God presides in the divine assembly. Among the gods, He renders ___

cards.text: Then God speaks, and He opens with a question. You ever get called into a meeting and the boss starts with "How long are we gonna keep doing this?" NOBODY in that room is relaxed.

cards.question: In the divine assembly, God asks how long they'll keep doing something. What is it?

answers.text: Judging unjustly and favoring the wicked
Ignoring the feasts and the sacrifices
Refusing to hear any cases at all

cards.text: So what SHOULD they be doing? No riddles. No hints. God LAYS. IT. OUT.

cards.question: God tells the assembly whose cause to defend. Whose is it?
God tells the assembly to rescue the weak and needy and save them from the hand of the wicked.

cards.text: Then comes a heavy line. They don't know, they don't understand, and they wander in the darkness. I know dark, friend. I did YEARS in the back of a junk drawer. Zero stars.

cards.question: While they wander in the darkness, all the foundations of the earth are ___

cards.text: Now God reminds them what He has said about them. And friend, it's a BIG title. Bigger than Papa, and I LOVE being Papa.

cards.question: In the divine assembly, God reminds them what He has said they are. What is it?

answers.text: Gods and sons of the Most High
Priests and servants of the temple

cards.text: Then comes one little word: But. You ever hear "You're doing great, but"? Friend, everything before that but just packed up and left the building.

cards.question: Big title and all, what does God say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will be scattered among the nations
They will be turned into servants

cards.question: God also tells them that like rulers they will fall.

cards.text: Then the psalm turns. It stops reporting on the assembly and calls out to God Himself to arise.

cards.question: The psalm asks God to arise and judge only the nation of Israel.
The psalm calls on God to judge the earth. What reason does it give?

answers.text: All the nations are His inheritance
The rulers have all stepped down
The nations have asked Him to

findings.problem: The joke invents a new moment in the Millers' kitchen (the family getting serious when somebody touched the last cookie). That moment isn't in the backstory, and the Millers' kitchen isn't his bakery, which is the only place his jokes may make up small moments and habits.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from Psalm 82:3. It is only a joke and a lead-in, yet it cites Psalm 82:3. It doesn't move the passage forward, and its citation is wider than what it uses. It also adds a third beat-free card between choices without carrying any part of the text.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites Psalm 82:3 but uses none of that verse.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "While they wander in the darkness" adds a time link between the two clauses of Psalm 82:5. The text only sets them side by side with a semicolon and doesn't say how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 2's question already says the assembly is made up of "the gods" (Among the gods, He renders ___), and card 10 hints at a title bigger than Papa. That makes "Gods and sons of the Most High" an instant pick over the prophet and priest answers. Card 11 either needs a different question or the earlier cards need rewording so they don't hand over the answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
